statement: A number has two digits. Its digits add to 7, and the digit on the left is twice the digit on the right. What is the number?

choices.misconception: I made the digits add to 7 but did not check which digit was the larger one.
I made the digits add to 7 but got the doubling the wrong way round.
I made the digits add to 7 but the left digit is not twice the right one.
I made the digits add to 7 but doubled the wrong digit.

hints: List every pair of digits that adds to seven.
Write out the pairs that add to 7, then test each pair against the second clue. Only one pair has a left digit that is exactly double the right digit.
The pairs adding to 7 are 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4, and 4 and 3.

solutions.reliable: The digit pairs adding to 7 are 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4. Only 4 and 3 has the left digit twice the right, so the number is 43. The idea to keep: use the first clue to make a short list, then test the list against the second clue rather than guessing.

whyOnTest: Checking a short list against a second clue is how early digit puzzles are solved, and every distractor satisfies one clue but not both.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
